programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ bèicearachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Beth agus Isaac cuide ri Linda agus iad a’ fuine cèic le cnò-chòco agus smeuragan. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad dèanamh cinnteach gu bheil a h-uile cail tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha smeuragan a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson a’ cheic a dhèanamh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe! Linda Macleod and friends cook a number of tasty dishes. She is joined by Beth and Isaac to bake a delicious coconut and blackberry cake. However, before they start, they must be sure they have all the ingredients. If not, they make a list and go shopping. Linda and her friends also find out more about how blackberries are grown, and then it's back into the kitchen to bake the cake before sitting down at the table to taste it.

programme.title: Oscar & Ealasaid
programme.desc: Tha Oscar a’ coinneachadh ri Raghgan, seann charaid a chleachd a bhith a’ cluich ceòl còmhla ris. Tha Raghgan airson ’s gun tèid an dithis aca air chuairt còmhla a-rithist, ach dè idir a nì Ealasaid às aonais Oscar? Ernest meets his old friend Léon, who he played music with when he was young. Léon insists that Ernest accompanies him on tour again, but what will Célestine do without Ernest?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Nìp a’ lorg chuibhlichean. Tha Tilidh a’ lorg chuibhlichean. Mu dheireadh thall, tha Àtaidh a’ lorg chuibhlichean dha fhèin. Chan eil iad cho cumhachdach an toiseach, ach chan fhada gus am fàs iad ro chumhachdach fiù ’s! Neep and Teal find some wheels. Finally, Abney gets hold of some wheels of his own. They aren't brilliant at first, but soon they become perhaps even a bit too brilliant!

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha thìd ann airson facal Abadas ùr agus turas 'aba-do-be-dee' ùr cuideachd! An-diugh, 's e 'bior-deighe' am facal. Tha na h-Abadas ag ionnsachadh gu bheil ceangal aige ri uisge, ach càite an lorg iad e agus cò bu chòir a dhol ga lorg? It is time for a new Abada word and a new 'aba-do-be-dee' adventure. This time the word is 'icicle'. The Abadas learn that it has something to do with water, but where will they find it and who should go on the adventure?

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Ball-coise air BBC ALBA/Football on BBC ALBA
programme.desc: An dàrna geam’ eadar Stenhousemuir agus Alloa Athletic ann an cuairt dheireannach play-off an Championship. Am prògram slàn air BBC ALBA air a’ lìbhrigeadh le Derek MacAoidh agus an sgioba aithris, Ailig O’Henley agus John Rankin. The second leg of the Championship play-off final between Stenhousemuir and Alloa Athletic. Full match coverage on BBC ALBA with presenter Derek MacKay and the commentary team of Alex O’Henley and John Rankin.

programme.title: Prosbaig
programme.desc: Bho mheadhan nan 80an bha am prògram telebhisein Prosbaig a' sgrùdadh chùisean na Gàidhealtachd 's nan Eilean, agus Alba san fharsaingeachd. Tron t-sreath seo, tha am fear-naidheachd Dòmhnall Moireasdan a' toirt sùil air ais tron tasglann agus a' toirt thugainn taghadh de na sgeulachdan a chaidh a chraoladh eadar 1984 agus 1988. Anns a' phrògram seo: làithean geala Sgioba Ball-coise Nis os cionn chàich anns na h-eileanan - air a' phàirc agus dhith; an Leòdhasach òg bhon a' Bhac a bha a' cluiche do Chaley Inbhir Nis; agus mar a chaidh cliù lus nan laogh ma sgaoil. From the mid-1980s, Gaelic current affairs television series Prosbaig covered many of the main stories making headlines in the Highlands and Islands and throughout Scotland. Journalist Donald Morrison takes a look back through the archive and brings us some of the key stories from 1984 to 1988. In this programme: the success of island team Ness FC; a look at life for a young boy from Back selected to play for Inverness Caley; and an innovative health remedy makes headlines!

programme.title: Mach à Seo!
programme.desc: Ramsay travels to Ayrshire for a busy and exhilarating few days. Sgrìob gu ruige Siorrachd Àir le Ramsay son là neo dhà làn spòrs.

programme.title: Immigration Tracks
programme.desc: From Canada's Eastern province of Cape Breton, we embark on a road-trip east to Toronto, Ontario, in search of Scottish Gaelic families who settled in this vast country over 100 years ago. Anne arrives in Toronto, a city with rich historic links to Scottish immigrants. She meets a Gaelic online publisher and takes to the ice at the Hockey Hall of Fame. How do generations of Canadian Scots identify with their roots? Join Anne McAlpine on a cultural voyage of discovery. Anns an earrann mu dheireadh seo, tha Anne air Toronto a ruighinn, baile le dlùth cheangal eachdraidheil ri in-immrichean Albannach. Thèid Anne a chèilidh air foillsichear air loidhne agus bidh i cuideachd a’ tadhal air Talla nan Laoch Hocaidh, ach saoil dè mar thèid dhith fhèin air an deigh?

programme.title: Ar Ceol 2024 | Scotland in Music
programme.desc: Tha Megan NicGill-Fhaolain a’ toirt thugainn cruinneachadh dhen cheòl beò as fheàrr bho na tachartasan-ciùil as motha ann an Alba ann an 2024. Le ceòl a chaidh a chlàradh gu h-àraidh aig Celtic Connections, a’ chuirm iongantach a bh’ aig Skipinnish aig Caisteal Dhùn Èidinn a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna, agus dhà dhen na tachartasan ciùil as motha dhen bhliadhna – Duaisean Na Trads agus Hoolie 2024. Megan MacLellan presents highlights from another year of amazing live music in Scotland from some of the country’s top events in 2024. Featuring bespoke recordings and gig footage from Celtic Connections, and coverage from Skipinnish’s incredible 25th anniversary show at Edinburgh Castle as well as two of the biggest traditional music events of the year - The Trad Awards and Hoolie 2024. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Famous Five
programme.desc: An sgeulachd iongantach aig Smith, Johnstone, Reilly, Turnbull agus Ormond; an loidhne-aghaidh iomraiteach no am "Famous Five" aig Hibernian FC a chuir ball-coise na h-Alba fon casan sna bliadhnaichean as dèidh an dara cogaidh. The remarkable story of Smith, Johnstone, Reilly, Turnbull and Ormond, Hibernian FC's talented 'Famous Five' forward line, which dominated Scottish football in the post-war period.

programme.title: Sgeulachd Cogaidh na h-Artaig/Untold Arctic Wars
programme.desc: The United States increases its activities in Greenland, the Soviet Union opens a new nuclear test site in the north, and the scale of nuclear testing grows.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Ross Miller Band, clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads, 2025. A’ gabhail a-steach The Dedication Jigs agus The Drunken Man from Kalabakan. Concert set performed by the Ross Miller Band, originally recorded live at the Trad Awards, 2025. Featured tracks include The Dedication Jigs and The Drunken Man from Kalabakan.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Angus Mackay is joined by close friend Finlay Macleod from Scalpay for the final fishing trip of the season. With summer fading, the environment looks very different as the purple heather really comes to the fore. Tracked by the golden eagle, they sail north to the hamlet of Calbost to take advantage of the shelter offered by its bay on a less than optimal day. As the duo fish in the bay, they ponder the extremes of the sea - its matchless beauty and its mortal danger. Anns a’ phrògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha Fionnlagh MacLeòid à Sgalpaigh, còmhla ri Aonghas airson an turas iasgaich mu dheireadh den t-seusan. Leis an samhradh a’ tighinn gu crìoch, tha an àrainneachd a’ coimhead gu math eadar-dhealaichte, ‘s am fraoch purpaidh a’ tighinn am follais. Air an leantainn le iolaire-bhuidhe, seòlaidh iad gu tuath, gu Calbost gus beagan fasgadh fhaighinn sa bhàgh, air latha meadhanach grod. Fhad ’s a tha iad ag iasgach, tha iad a’ meòrachadh air an dà chuid cunnart agus bòidhchead na mara.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Tha Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ air Falasgair gu Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House agus an còmhlan nua-trad Sgìtheanach a’ cur a’ chiad latha de Belladrum 2025 gu dol. Ged nach do thòisich iad gu 2022, tha an còmhlan air iad fhèin a stèidheachadh gu sgiobalta air cuairt nam fèisean leis a’ cheòl bheothail aca agus duaisean am pailteas air a choisinn air an t-slighe. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome Falasgair to the Hot House Stage as the contemporary trad band from Skye light up the opening day. Launched in 2022, the band members have quickly established themselves on the festival circuit with their high-energy music and have won a raft of awards along the way.

programme.title: The Teachers' Lounge
programme.desc: Carla Nowak (Leonie Benesch) is a dedicated, idealistic young teacher in her first job at a German middle school. Her relaxed rapport with her seventh-grade students is put under stress when a series of thefts occur at the school, and a staff investigation leads to accusations and mistrust among outraged parents, opinionated colleagues and angry students. Caught in the middle of these complex dynamics, Carla tries to mediate, but the more she tries to do everything right, the more desperate her position becomes. In German with English subtitles.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth is dreading being invited to Onslow's birthday party almost as much as he dreads her agreeing to come. However, she changes her mind when she learns that Rose's new boyfriend, a well-to-do Greek businessman, will be picking her and Richard up from their home in his limousine. In true Hyacinth fashion, she decides to hold a cocktails and canapes party starting an hour before the limousine's planned arrival time so that the invited crowd will see the prestigious form of transport being used. Sadly, things do not go quite as she expected...

programme.title: Sorry!
programme.desc: Mother is out to get Aunt Esme's money for Timothy, and Timothy has encounters with a garage owner and his dogs.

programme.title: Ian Hislop Goes off the Rails
programme.desc: Ian Hislop brings his customary humour, analysis and wit to the notorious Beeching Report of 1963, which led to the closure of a third of the nation's railway lines and stations and forced tens of thousands of people into the car and onto the road. Was author Dr Richard Beeching little more than Genghis Khan with a slide rule, ruthlessly hacking away at Britain's rail network in a misguided quest for profitability, or was he the fall guy for short-sighted government policies that favoured the car over the train? Ian also investigates the fallout of Beeching's plan, discovering what was lost to the British landscape, communities and ways of life when the railway map shrank, and recalls the halcyon days of train travel, celebrated by John Betjeman. Ian travels from Cornwall to the Scottish borders, meeting those responsible and those affected and questioning whether such brutal measures could be justified. Knowing what we know now, with trains far more energy efficient and environmentally sound than cars, perhaps Beeching's plan was the biggest folly of the 1960s?

And Paul Carter meets the robodog helping to analyse plants and crops.

programme.title: Rachel Khoo's Kitchen Notebook
programme.desc: In this colourful episode, Rachel explores the fast-paced streets of Naples and feels the heat in the kitchen of a very particular pizza chef. She learns how to make a traditional pizza and discovers some new flavours which inspire her to put her own 'Khoo-twist' on the Italian dishes she's tasted. Back home in London, Rachel cooks food inspired by her trip to Naples, including ricotta and gorgonzola sfogliatelle, pasta pizza and shake-and-make ice-cream.

programme.title: World Questions
programme.desc: Migration, citizenship laws, crime and the rising cost of living - just some of the issues facing voters in Sweden. World Questions visits the country's capital, Stockholm, to debate the challenges facing the nation ahead of upcoming elections. Leading politicians will face questions from a Swedish audience in a discussion chaired by Jonny Dymond.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Munya Chawawa found viral fame during the lockdown for his satirical videos on social media. Now he has a new Channel 4 documentary, Wrestling with Trump, which looks at the links between professional wrestling and the MAGA movement. Restrictions on prisoners in the UK speaking to journalists are in focus after the Guardian was told Jeremy Bamber can no longer exchange letters or phone calls with journalists. Bamber was convicted in 1986 of murdering his adoptive family and is serving life in prison. Simon Hattenstone, feature writer at the Guardian, and Emily Bolton, defence lawyer and founder of Objection, set out the issues. The top parenting influencers, often dubbed as “momfluencers”, can earn millions. The phenomena is the subject of a new book, Like, Follow, Subscribe: Influencer Kids and the Cost of a Childhood Online. Its author, Fortesa Latifi, and Jasmine McInnes, family and travel influencer, discuss the world of “sharenting”.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: This year, the Finnish city of Oulu is European Capital of Culture. The Nordic country is consistently ranked as the happiest place on earth, despite shivering in sub-zero temperatures for many months of the year. So could its culture be the reason why? Rob Bells heads to Oulu to see how warmly people there embrace the snow and ice, travels deep into Lapland to see how children visiting Santa Claus have transformed the region and sees for himself the deep bond between the Lapps and their reindeer.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Munya Chawawa found viral fame during the lockdown for his satirical videos on social media. Now he has a new Channel 4 documentary, Wrestling with Trump, which looks at the links between professional wrestling and the MAGA movement. Restrictions on prisoners in the UK speaking to journalists are in focus after the Guardian was told Jeremy Bamber can no longer exchange letters or phone calls with journalists. Bamber was convicted in 1986 of murdering his adoptive family and is serving life in prison. Simon Hattenstone, feature writer at the Guardian, and Emily Bolton, defence lawyer and founder of Objection, set out the issues. The top parenting influencers, often dubbed as “momfluencers”, can earn millions. The phenomena is the subject of a new book, Like, Follow, Subscribe: Influencer Kids and the Cost of a Childhood Online. Its author, Fortesa Latifi, and Jasmine McInnes, family and travel influencer, discuss the world of “sharenting”.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Live coverage of the 2025/26 FA Cup final between Chelsea and Manchester City from Wembley Stadium. Manchester City are the first club in history to reach the final four years in a row, but they were beaten by Manchester United in 2024 and by Crystal Palace in 2025. Under Pep Guardiola, they have lifted the famous old trophy on two occasions, in 2019 and 2023. Chelsea’s last FA Cup win came in 2018 when they beat Manchester United. It’s been a turbulent season for the club, with managers Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior both being sacked, so the FA Cup represents a last shot at silverware. Manchester City are chasing a Wembley double having already claimed the League Cup this season. These two teams have won the FA Cup 15 times between them but have never faced each other in an FA Cup final.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team of soap stars – Nick Pickard from Hollyoaks, Coronation Street's Sue Cleaver, Emmerdale's Rebecca Sarker and Perry Fenwick from EastEnders – taking on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Blankety Blank
programme.desc: The legendary Blankety Blank is back! Bradley Walsh hosts as a panel of six celebrities fill in the missing blanks and help win some brilliant prizes for some very lucky contestants. This week, he’s joined by Kym Marsh, Jenny Ryan, Babatunde Aleshe, Chris McCausland, Michael Dapaah and Chizzy Akudolu.

programme.title: The Weakest Link
programme.desc: Romesh Ranganathan is back quizzing eight celebrities who are all after a potential prize pot of £50,000 for their charity. Initially working together, the celebrities must vote off the weakest link each round until just two remain in the head-to-head. But only one can claim the prize. The celebrity contestants in this episode are Jill Scott, Laura Tobin, Nella Rose, Simon Rimmer, Jaz Singh, Stephen Bailey, Joel Corry and Kate Quilton.

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Live coverage of the 2025/26 FA Cup final between Chelsea and Manchester City from Wembley Stadium. Manchester City are the first club in history to reach the final four years in a row, but they were beaten by Manchester United in 2024 and by Crystal Palace in 2025. Under Pep Guardiola, they have lifted the famous old trophy on two occasions, in 2019 and 2023. Chelsea’s last FA Cup win came in 2018 when they beat Manchester United. It’s been a turbulent season for the club, with managers Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior both being sacked, so the FA Cup represents a last shot at silverware. Manchester City are chasing a Wembley double having already claimed the League Cup this season. These two teams have won the FA Cup 15 times between them but have never faced each other in an FA Cup final.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Live coverage of the 2025/26 FA Cup final between Chelsea and Manchester City from Wembley Stadium. Manchester City are the first club in history to reach the final four years in a row, but they were beaten by Manchester United in 2024 and by Crystal Palace in 2025. Under Pep Guardiola, they have lifted the famous old trophy on two occasions, in 2019 and 2023. Chelsea’s last FA Cup win came in 2018 when they beat Manchester United. It’s been a turbulent season for the club, with managers Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior both being sacked, so the FA Cup represents a last shot at silverware. Manchester City are chasing a Wembley double having already claimed the League Cup this season. These two teams have won the FA Cup 15 times between them but have never faced each other in an FA Cup final.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team of soap stars – Nick Pickard from Hollyoaks, Coronation Street's Sue Cleaver, Emmerdale's Rebecca Sarker and Perry Fenwick from EastEnders – taking on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Blankety Blank
programme.desc: The legendary Blankety Blank is back! Bradley Walsh hosts as a panel of six celebrities fill in the missing blanks and help win some brilliant prizes for some very lucky contestants. This week, he’s joined by Kym Marsh, Jenny Ryan, Babatunde Aleshe, Chris McCausland, Michael Dapaah and Chizzy Akudolu.

programme.title: The Weakest Link
programme.desc: Romesh Ranganathan is back quizzing eight celebrities who are all after a potential prize pot of £50,000 for their charity. Initially working together, the celebrities must vote off the weakest link each round until just two remain in the head-to-head. But only one can claim the prize. The celebrity contestants in this episode are Jill Scott, Laura Tobin, Nella Rose, Simon Rimmer, Jaz Singh, Stephen Bailey, Joel Corry and Kate Quilton.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team of soap stars – Nick Pickard from Hollyoaks, Coronation Street's Sue Cleaver, Emmerdale's Rebecca Sarker and Perry Fenwick from EastEnders – taking on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Live coverage of the 2025/26 FA Cup final between Chelsea and Manchester City from Wembley Stadium. Manchester City are the first club in history to reach the final four years in a row, but they were beaten by Manchester United in 2024 and by Crystal Palace in 2025. Under Pep Guardiola, they have lifted the famous old trophy on two occasions, in 2019 and 2023. Chelsea’s last FA Cup win came in 2018 when they beat Manchester United. It’s been a turbulent season for the club, with managers Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior both being sacked, so the FA Cup represents a last shot at silverware. Manchester City are chasing a Wembley double having already claimed the League Cup this season. These two teams have won the FA Cup 15 times between them but have never faced each other in an FA Cup final.

programme.title: The Weakest Link

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Live coverage of the 2025/26 FA Cup final between Chelsea and Manchester City from Wembley Stadium. Manchester City are the first club in history to reach the final four years in a row, but they were beaten by Manchester United in 2024 and by Crystal Palace in 2025. Under Pep Guardiola, they have lifted the famous old trophy on two occasions, in 2019 and 2023. Chelsea’s last FA Cup win came in 2018 when they beat Manchester United. It’s been a turbulent season for the club, with managers Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior both being sacked, so the FA Cup represents a last shot at silverware. Manchester City are chasing a Wembley double having already claimed the League Cup this season. These two teams have won the FA Cup 15 times between them but have never faced each other in an FA Cup final.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team of soap stars – Nick Pickard from Hollyoaks, Coronation Street's Sue Cleaver, Emmerdale's Rebecca Sarker and Perry Fenwick from EastEnders – taking on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Gary McAllister made the game of football look easy. The proverbial classy midfield player who saw the full picture, and could affect it, in the crucial seconds before his opponent. Unprepared to succumb to a story that began with knock-backs, Gary wrote his own place in the history and folklore of every club he played for - a winner at Motherwell, champion at Leeds, immortal at Liverpool, and a Scotland captain of some repute. But there were lows to counter the highs, and Gary discusses these with searing honesty. However, he is not defined by the hard times, but rather the moments where his class and will to win elevated him to the very top of the game. With contributions from Steven Gerrard, Gordon Strachan and Ardal O’Hanlon, this is the story of one of the greatest Scotland players of his, or any, generation.

programme.title: Scotland's Home of the Year
programme.desc: In the north east and northern isles, the judges must choose between a reimagined rural house in Aberdeenshire, a converted crofter's house on Shetland and a modern newbuild in Chapleton. Scoring them on architectural merit, distinctive design and personal style, which home will Anna, Banjo and Danny judge worthy enough to go forward to the grand final?

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: This is an average story of a very average woman. Of Spud, carer for her father, who cooks, cleans and serves badly and half-heartedly. A woman who is never seen or thanked. Ignored. A woman who, in spite of what society tells her, does not feel bad about herself. Who despite not being young, or a mother, or worst of all, beautiful, is actually quite happy in herself, if not her life. Then, one day, everything changes, and Siobhan may have to come out of the shadows and be seen.

programme.desc: What will the Doctor find at the end of the universe? Listen! What scares the Doctor? programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: When the ghosts try to sabotage Alison’s makeshift therapy session for Kitty, they unwittingly face their own demons. Mike’s desire to see the ghosts yields surprising results.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: As Alison spends more and more time with Lucy, she has to have a frank talk with Kitty about her feelings of jealousy. The Captain offers Kitty a shoulder to cry on, but in doing so unearths an inconsistency that needs explaining. Luckily Lady Button has recently become a sleuthing expert, so the Captain recruits her to help uncover the truth. Meanwhile, Pat leads Mary and Robin in an improvisation class with varying success, and Thomas is determined to show off his football skills to impress Alison, but Humphrey’s Head is not best pleased that he will have to 'play ball' – literally. While Julian helps (and hinders) Mike to film a promo video for the house using a fancy yet unruly drone camera, the Captain, Kitty and Lady Button work together with the other ghosts to solve the unfolding mystery they’ve discovered before it’s too late and all at Button House is lost.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: After a spate of burglaries in Finglas, Agnes asks Buster Brady to fit a new alarm system. Unfortunately there are a few teething problems with Buster's state-of-the-art technology. Determined to help son Dermot set up a new business, Agnes must face old rival Hillary Nicholson in the poker final. Meanwhile, Agnes's new chair turns out to be comfier than she could ever have imagined...

programme.desc: Liko and Meowscarada face off against a fellow Nidothing fan who really loves Litten.

programme.title: Bro's in Control
programme.desc: Callum has taken Adam and Joe’s phones, and they must abseil down the world's tallest abseil tower to get them back. Meanwhile, Joel M teaches Joe a trick or two about disappearing.

programme.title: Gladiators: Epic Pranks
programme.desc: Daring each other with silly in-ear prompts, Apollo, Hammer, Nitro and Fire go head-to-head at a fitness studio. Who will rack up enough prank points to win?

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Joel and Abby take on a high-speed rally racing challenge, and as excitement builds around the Eurovision Song Contest, UK contender Look Mum No Computer and 2025 entry Remember Monday join us in studio!

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Bill Bailey introduces a delightfully eccentric cast of creatures that have chosen to do things differently. Odd, unconventional and unusual - these are animals that don't normally grab the limelight. They include the parrot that has forgotten how to fly, the bear that has turned vegetarian, a chameleon that is barely bigger than an ant, and a penguin that lives in a forest. Nature's Misfits reveals the extraordinary and rarely seen lives of these evolutionary oddballs along with their strange habitats, unusual forms and the incredible hurdles they overcome.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With the promise of warmer days ahead, Monty makes a start on planting up some of his spectacular summer containers. He’s also got leeks to plant out and shares some advice on how to make your own fertiliser. Frances Tophill heads to Berkshire to learn more about biodynamic gardening and the benefits it can bring. It’s also time for an update from Adam Frost’s new garden, where things are slowly starting to take shape. In Cumbria, a couple of growers share their love of auriculas as they get ready for this year’s RHS Chelsea Flower Show. And as part of Mental Health Awareness Week, a forager explains how her garden helped her to heal after being diagnosed with cancer.

programme.title: How to Marry a Millionaire
programme.desc: Three New York models, looking for rich husbands, rent a luxurious apartment together to impress affluent bachelors, but things do not go to plan.

programme.title: Athletics: Diamond League
programme.desc: Coverage of the athletics competition featuring the world's greatest athletes.

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: Andi Oliver travels to the north east of England, to the fishing town of Bridlington, where she uncovers its best-kept secret – it’s the lobster capital of Europe! Andi wants to put on a party that not only gets the word out about Bridlington’s extraordinary, little-known claim to fame but also helps to secure the future of its historic fishing industry. The fleet are worried that not enough young people are taking an interest in what happens at the busy harbour, but will Andi’s plans to take the town’s teenagers on a fishing trip in choppy waters really convince them to sign up for a career on the high seas? To get the whole town excited about the lobster caught on their doorstep, Andi must come up with a shellfish feast that appeals to all and a spectacular way to make a big noise about it. This means drawing on the expertise of brilliant local chefs and sourcing delicious regional produce. But is a New Orleans-style parade the best way to get the locals crazy about lobster, and will the young people of Bridlington even show up to try it?

programme.title: Great Bear Stakeout
programme.desc: In this episode we meet Parsnip, a first-time grizzly mum, and her young cub, Pushki. Only half of new bear cubs make it through the season, and they are both struggling to survive in this vast Alaskan wilderness. This area is ruled by a massive male bear, Van, and his partner Alice, a prized female bear with an aggressive and sinister side. Hungry adult bears will kill cubs, so Parsnip's summer is full of unexpected adventure; she must escape Van's clutches and learn from her mistakes if she and her cub are to survive the season.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A young canine-loving couple from Hertfordshire are hoping for a fresh start in a new High Weald home. Their budget is £600,000, and Ginny Buckley has some tempting properties to show them. Away from the houses, Ginny picks some of the local grape harvest before treating herself to a glass of fizz.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Capesthorne Hall in Cheshire. Hundreds of visitors arrive with their family heirlooms, and the experts pick out the best items to go off to auction. Paul Martin investigates the history of nearby Quarrybank Mill.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two of Britain’s best-loved actors, Peter Gunn and Melanie Hill, venture through Staffordshire and Derbyshire to find antiques they can flip for a profit. Swapping Coronation Street’s cobbles for antique shops, they’re joined by experts James Braxton and David Harper. Peter and Melanie’s 30-year friendship is put to one side as they become rivals. Armed with £400 and a classic car, they have just two days to find the best antiques to sell at auction.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a fragile silk robe and a wartime wall painting to a writer’s handmade timepiece, the hidden treasures in these two houses reveal the stories of two of Britain’s most celebrated authors – and the expert teams racing to preserve them.

programme.title: Darkest Hour
programme.desc: May 1940. As the Nazis advance against Britain's European allies, newly elected prime minister Winston Churchill must decide whether to leave neighbouring countries to their fate by striking a peace deal with Hitler, or fight on against terrifying odds for the greater good.

programme.title: Their Finest
programme.desc: 1940, London, the Blitz. With the country's morale at stake, Catrin, an untried screenwriter from Ebbw Vale, and a makeshift cast and crew work under fire to make a film to lift the nation's spirits - and inspire America to join the war. Leading the cast is the self-absorbed actor Ambrose Hilliard, who is persuaded to coach the handsome young American hero who has been 'parachuted' into the acting profession - but that will only be when the script is produced. Acclaimed period drama from BBC Films.

programme.title: LGBTQ+ Hits at the BBC
programme.desc: Join us for this celebration of pop’s greatest LGBTQ+ stars whose gender and sexuality are central to the story of their individual careers and the amazing songs they have created. Our rainbow alliance of amazing artists includes George Michael, Boy George, Freddie Mercury, Beth Ditto, MNEK, Lil Nas X and Barry Manilow. Some pushed boundaries and challenged gender stereotypes from the very start, others only revealed their true selves after years of success and speculation – but all have played their part in changing the world of popular music and the sounds that we listen to and love.

programme.title: Half Man
programme.desc: 1993. Niall is conflicted when asked by his mother to lie in court about Ruben’s violence. Ruben seems to have changed for the better, so the decision weighs heavily on him.

programme.title: To Think Like a Killer
programme.desc: Ann’s landmark study reshapes criminal investigation. Serial crime falls, but the battle is only just beginning.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: The week closes with the third quarter-final as the six best cooks of the week return, taking on two more challenges to prove they have the nerve and skill to go even further.

Their budget is £600,000, and Ginny Buckley has some tempting properties to show them. Away from the houses, Ginny picks some of the local grape harvest before treating herself to a glass of fizz.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Capesthorne Hall in Cheshire. Hundreds of visitors arrive with their family heirlooms, and the experts pick out the best items to go off to auction. Paul Martin investigates the history of nearby Quarrybank Mill.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two of Britain’s best-loved actors, Peter Gunn and Melanie Hill, venture through Staffordshire and Derbyshire to find antiques they can flip for a profit. Swapping Coronation Street’s cobbles for antique shops, they’re joined by experts James Braxton and David Harper. Peter and Melanie’s 30-year friendship is put to one side as they become rivals. Armed with £400 and a classic car, they have just two days to find the best antiques to sell at auction.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a fragile silk robe and a wartime wall painting to a writer’s handmade timepiece, the hidden treasures in these two houses reveal the stories of two of Britain’s most celebrated authors – and the expert teams racing to preserve them.

programme.title: Darkest Hour
programme.desc: May 1940. As the Nazis advance against Britain's European allies, newly elected prime minister Winston Churchill must decide whether to leave neighbouring countries to their fate by striking a peace deal with Hitler, or fight on against terrifying odds for the greater good.

programme.title: Their Finest
programme.desc: 1940, London, the Blitz. With the country's morale at stake, Catrin, an untried screenwriter from Ebbw Vale, and a makeshift cast and crew work under fire to make a film to lift the nation's spirits - and inspire America to join the war. Leading the cast is the self-absorbed actor Ambrose Hilliard, who is persuaded to coach the handsome young American hero who has been 'parachuted' into the acting profession - but that will only be when the script is produced. Acclaimed period drama from BBC Films.

programme.title: LGBTQ+ Hits at the BBC
programme.desc: Join us for this celebration of pop’s greatest LGBTQ+ stars whose gender and sexuality are central to the story of their individual careers and the amazing songs they have created. Our rainbow alliance of amazing artists includes George Michael, Boy George, Freddie Mercury, Beth Ditto, MNEK, Lil Nas X and Barry Manilow. Some pushed boundaries and challenged gender stereotypes from the very start, others only revealed their true selves after years of success and speculation – but all have played their part in changing the world of popular music and the sounds that we listen to and love.

programme.title: Half Man
programme.desc: 1993. Niall is conflicted when asked by his mother to lie in court about Ruben’s violence. Ruben seems to have changed for the better, so the decision weighs heavily on him.

programme.title: To Think Like a Killer
programme.desc: Ann’s landmark study reshapes criminal investigation. Serial crime falls, but the battle is only just beginning.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: The week closes with the third quarter-final as the six best cooks of the week return, taking on two more challenges to prove they have the nerve and skill to go even further.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Halfway through the week, TV icon Anneka Rice, comedian Shane Todd and Radio 1Xtra DJ Remi Burgz face a fresh test of knowledge. Vernon Kay puts the spotlight onto his home town of Bolton, while unreliable guide Paul Gorton delivers the tour, complete with a few extra treats along the way.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Exhausted with requests for help, Looph deliberately disappears. The Piris turn detective, searching the berg with little success until her ingenious plan is finally revealed.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: When Cosima wrongly accuses Big Lizard of eating Dad's birthday cake, he vanishes. Has he run away, or is he planning a special surprise to save the day?

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings try to get rid of a bat that has interrupted their game. But Weasy thinks it's supercool and ditches the ducklings to become a comic book hero with a bat sidekick.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: To avoid Herbert’s surprise visits via his tunnels in the Big Birch, the other heroes take any quest and must deal with an angry plant!

programme.desc: Grizzy and the Lemmings discover a school of crabs that live in an underwater city.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck and Frog have a job tidying the mayor’s garden, but then Frog builds an automatic lawnmower, which soon causes chaos. Can Duck get everything back on track in time?

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Liko and Meowscarada face off against a fellow Nidothing fan who really loves Litten.

programme.title: Bro's in Control
programme.desc: Callum has taken Adam and Joe’s phones, and they must abseil down the world's tallest abseil tower to get them back. Meanwhile, Joel M teaches Joe a trick or two about disappearing.

programme.title: Gladiators: Epic Pranks
programme.desc: Daring each other with silly in-ear prompts, Apollo, Hammer, Nitro and Fire go head-to-head at a fitness studio. Who will rack up enough prank points to win?

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Joel and Abby take on a high-speed rally racing challenge, and as excitement builds around the Eurovision Song Contest, UK contender Look Mum No Computer and 2025 entry Remember Monday join us in studio!

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Bill Bailey introduces a delightfully eccentric cast of creatures that have chosen to do things differently. Odd, unconventional and unusual - these are animals that don't normally grab the limelight. They include the parrot that has forgotten how to fly, the bear that has turned vegetarian, a chameleon that is barely bigger than an ant, and a penguin that lives in a forest. Nature's Misfits reveals the extraordinary and rarely seen lives of these evolutionary oddballs along with their strange habitats, unusual forms and the incredible hurdles they overcome.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With the promise of warmer days ahead, Monty makes a start on planting up some of his spectacular summer containers. He’s also got leeks to plant out and shares some advice on how to make your own fertiliser. Frances Tophill heads to Berkshire to learn more about biodynamic gardening and the benefits it can bring. It’s also time for an update from Adam Frost’s new garden, where things are slowly starting to take shape. In Cumbria, a couple of growers share their love of auriculas as they get ready for this year’s RHS Chelsea Flower Show. And as part of Mental Health Awareness Week, a forager explains how her garden helped her to heal after being diagnosed with cancer.

programme.title: How to Marry a Millionaire
programme.desc: Three New York models, looking for rich husbands, rent a luxurious apartment together to impress affluent bachelors, but things do not go to plan.

programme.title: Athletics: Diamond League
programme.desc: Coverage of the athletics competition featuring the world's greatest athletes.

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: Andi Oliver travels to the north east of England, to the fishing town of Bridlington, where she uncovers its best-kept secret – it’s the lobster capital of Europe! Andi wants to put on a party that not only gets the word out about Bridlington’s extraordinary, little-known claim to fame but also helps to secure the future of its historic fishing industry. The fleet are worried that not enough young people are taking an interest in what happens at the busy harbour, but will Andi’s plans to take the town’s teenagers on a fishing trip in choppy waters really convince them to sign up for a career on the high seas? To get the whole town excited about the lobster caught on their doorstep, Andi must come up with a shellfish feast that appeals to all and a spectacular way to make a big noise about it. This means drawing on the expertise of brilliant local chefs and sourcing delicious regional produce. But is a New Orleans-style parade the best way to get the locals crazy about lobster, and will the young people of Bridlington even show up to try it?

programme.title: Great Bear Stakeout
programme.desc: In this episode we meet Parsnip, a first-time grizzly mum, and her young cub, Pushki. Only half of new bear cubs make it through the season, and they are both struggling to survive in this vast Alaskan wilderness. This area is ruled by a massive male bear, Van, and his partner Alice, a prized female bear with an aggressive and sinister side. Hungry adult bears will kill cubs, so Parsnip's summer is full of unexpected adventure; she must escape Van's clutches and learn from her mistakes if she and her cub are to survive the season.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Bill Bailey introduces a delightfully eccentric cast of creatures that have chosen to do things differently. Odd, unconventional and unusual - these are animals that don't normally grab the limelight. They include the parrot that has forgotten how to fly, the bear that has turned vegetarian, a chameleon that is barely bigger than an ant, and a penguin that lives in a forest. Nature's Misfits reveals the extraordinary and rarely seen lives of these evolutionary oddballs along with their strange habitats, unusual forms and the incredible hurdles they overcome.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With the promise of warmer days ahead, Monty makes a start on planting up some of his spectacular summer containers. He’s also got leeks to plant out and shares some advice on how to make your own fertiliser. Frances Tophill heads to Berkshire to learn more about biodynamic gardening and the benefits it can bring. It’s also time for an update from Adam Frost’s new garden, where things are slowly starting to take shape. In Cumbria, a couple of growers share their love of auriculas as they get ready for this year’s RHS Chelsea Flower Show. And as part of Mental Health Awareness Week, a forager explains how her garden helped her to heal after being diagnosed with cancer.

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: Andi Oliver travels to the north east of England, to the fishing town of Bridlington, where she uncovers its best-kept secret – it’s the lobster capital of Europe! Andi wants to put on a party that not only gets the word out about Bridlington’s extraordinary, little-known claim to fame but also helps to secure the future of its historic fishing industry. The fleet are worried that not enough young people are taking an interest in what happens at the busy harbour, but will Andi’s plans to take the town’s teenagers on a fishing trip in choppy waters really convince them to sign up for a career on the high seas? To get the whole town excited about the lobster caught on their doorstep, Andi must come up with a shellfish feast that appeals to all and a spectacular way to make a big noise about it. This means drawing on the expertise of brilliant local chefs and sourcing delicious regional produce. But is a New Orleans-style parade the best way to get the locals crazy about lobster, and will the young people of Bridlington even show up to try it?

programme.title: Great Bear Stakeout
programme.desc: In this episode we meet Parsnip, a first-time grizzly mum, and her young cub, Pushki. Only half of new bear cubs make it through the season, and they are both struggling to survive in this vast Alaskan wilderness. This area is ruled by a massive male bear, Van, and his partner Alice, a prized female bear with an aggressive and sinister side. Hungry adult bears will kill cubs, so Parsnip's summer is full of unexpected adventure; she must escape Van's clutches and learn from her mistakes if she and her cub are to survive the season.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After watching the birds fly above them, the Squirrels discover that birds can also slide, run and lay eggs. This encourages them to learn more about the natural environment, and they discover how to do this responsibly with Duggee’s five easy steps: watch carefully, stay at a distance, don’t interfere, be patient and alert, and stay quiet. The Squirrels embark on their own individual discoveries outside in rivers, the sea, mountains, the jungle and the desert. They learn how to spot an animal’s disguise, better known as its camouflage. They see how birds may try to impress one another, which is in stark contrast to how a horned lizard uses its body to warn other creatures off. A fascinating look at nature!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are hungry, but they’re not sure what to eat to fill their tummies, so they turn to Duggee for help. Fortunately, he has his cookbook The Clubhouse Kitchen: Tasty Bites for Hungry Squirrels, and together they pick out something they’d like. They decide the nut roast takes too long to make, and although cheetah toast is quicker, they don’t like getting raisins stuck in their teeth. Once they’ve picked a recipe, Duggee teaches them how to complete it: get the ingredients, prepare them and then put it together. After making some fun mess in the kitchen and a great cooking lesson, the Squirrels get to complete the last step together and eat what they made. Delicious!

Whether it's a perilous voyage to the bottom of the sea or the piratey pursuit of a giant squid, the Octonauts leap into action and always prove that eight heads are better than one. The Octonauts must help a giant sunfish who can't swim straight, before it hurts other sea creatures and itself.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Sunny meets his new baby sister, he’s disappointed that she can’t play all the games he had planned. But Vida knows just what to do - she teaches him how to spend time with a tiny baby, using Woolly the Caterpillar for practice.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Somebody stole the big hand off the clock tower. Mojo and Bo are on the case, but it is not as simple as it seems. Soon, they are pulling off a heist they never expected.

programme.title: Activate with Joe Wicks
programme.desc: Quietly, we approach this majestic beast... It's my Safari Squat Challenge! Can you tackle my big three? Squats, bear crawls and fast feet. The king of the jungle is the Activate! Get ready to move with Joe and the Activators.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Mr Tumble tries to keep quiet, as Grandad Tumble is sleeping. Justin and his friends do some quiet and loud dancing!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Forced to wait five minutes in front of a restaurant for their takeaway order, Bluey and Bingo become restless for entertainment, pushing the very limits of Dad’s patience.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum won’t let Bingo have pavlova, so the kids find a way by playing a cheeky game of cafe.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have just got some new walkie-talkies and are having so much fun with them. Duggee calls the Squirrels to come for some blueberry juice, but as Tag is running, he trips over a car and falls through a secret door in the wall! Communicating through his walkie-talkie, Tag doesn’t know where he is. He can see lots and lots of things around him but no one has any idea where this room is in the house!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: When the Squirrels search for Enid, they are surprised to hear her meow from the top of the Mighty Sugar Bun Mountain. The Squirrels prepare for the climb to rescue Enid, but first Duggee teaches them what they need to pack in their backpacks for a successful trip. The team walk through rocky terrain, grey skies, plentiful rain and snow blizzards but keep morale high as they learn how phrasing negative thoughts into helpful ones will let them overcome any challenges along the way. The Squirrels repeat their positive affirmations to keep climbing up the Sugar Bun as a team, and when they find themselves at the top of the mountain, they all give Enid a big hug. A successful rescue mission means Happy can have his nap on the sofa with Enid when they are back!

programme.title: Zog (Film)
programme.desc: A family film based on the much-loved picture book written by Julia Donaldson and illustrated by Axel Scheffler. The story of a keen young dragon who wants to learn how to fly, roar and breathe fire in his first years at Dragon School. He is desperate to impress his teacher and win a golden star, but he is accident-prone, and each year he has to be helped by a kind young girl who patches up his bumps and bruises. In year four, he has to capture a princess - can the young girl help him with his trickiest challenge yet? A Christmas viewing treat for all the family from four-time Oscar-nominated production company Magic Light Pictures. Featuring the voices of Sir Lenny Henry as the narrator, Hugh Skinner as Zog, Tracey Ullman as Madame Dragon, Patsy Ferran as Princess Pearl, Kit Harington as Sir Gadabout and some added vocals by Rob Brydon.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Kyan is invited to perform a dragon dance for Chinese New Year in Beijing. Glitch decides to build a fire-breathing dragon robot for the parade, and the Go Jetters need to stop it!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Can Weasy get his keepsakes back from the farmer's house?

programme.title: Spidey and His Amazing Friends
programme.desc: Zola is heroic. Aunt May's birthday balloon gets lost.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: While cleaning after a storm, the Octonauts find a primate known as a spectral tarsier.

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Peggy is judging an art contest, but a storm puts it in jeopardy. Can Stan save the day? And who will win the competition?

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Banana Superstar’s show is stopped when Evil Pea steals his peel. Supertato races against him to get it back, but trouble hits when a giant banana statue collapses onto the stage.

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: The Peak City Heroes are awarded the 'key to the city', but the ceremony gets interrupted.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: No, Rebecca isn’t wearing a box on her head - she’s dressed as an astronaut! This gives Murphi an idea. He helps Rebecca discover alien life by creating an alien out of a sock. The Mini Monsters are making skyscapes, Rebecca’s royal relative is looking for something, and the final mega monster make is another space-inspired creation. The Recycling Express and the Tiny Helpers support Rebecca and Murphi as they reach for the stars.

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Small is feeling very sleepy today. Jen is having fun with her marble run, but she’s missing a part. Doctor Dolly visits the cafe, Small flies off to see how broccoli grows, and the chefs whizz up a five-a-day pasta recipe for their kind guest.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk through a rainy forest to a hidden meadow. On the way, they cross a high bridge, discover a tree that’s been blown over by the wind, find a golf ball and even pretend to be raindrops!

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: Penny brings a dinosaur fossil to the nursery, while Bonnie and Hamish plan a secret dino dance. And mysterious footprints have Penny wondering if there’s a real dino on the island.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee uses his trusty binoculars to do some birdwatching, and of course the Squirrels want to have a go too. The problem is, if you want to go birdwatching you have to be very, very quiet, otherwise the birds will fly away. And being very, very quiet is difficult when you have Roly with you. Bird! Bird! Bird! Can Roly remember to whisper? And is Duggee's sneeze just a little too loud?

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Sunny doesn’t want to see the Sweetwood Band, even though he loves music, Vida helps him out with earmuffs and he gets to enjoy the show!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Animated adventure comedy series. It's Go Jetters glow when Glitch uses some glow-worms for his disco pizzazz in New Zealand.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi loves bouncing on the trampoline and wishes she could do it all day. Her feet become bouncy, and it's brilliant at first, until she realises that bouncing everywhere makes simple jobs tricky. Rafi doesn’t want any help, but soon she sees that bouncing all the time isn’t as fun as she thought. With her dads' support, she realises it’s okay to ask for help. Together, they share pancakes, laughter and a big upside-down hug.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Without her ukulele, Yukee struggles to come up with a tune for the words she wrote for a new song. Her friends try to help, but none of their styles fit. Can the piano Sonny and Paulie the peacock bring to the Sunhouse be the answer?

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: After a garden barbecue, Ziff, Pipp and Button turn straws and snacks into agility games.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends are at a campsite having lots of fun in the great outdoors. Mr Tumble and Tumble Ted go on a camping trip of their own, but has Mr Tumble remembered to pack everything?

programme.title: The Toddler Club
programme.desc: Gemma, Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear welcome toddlers Suuvi, Margot, Jasper, Sammie, Teddy and Tehrani, and their grown-ups, to the Toddler Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! The What’s in the Box? game reveals a toothbrush, and when the toddlers and parents open up a bigger box, they discover lots more objects and toys that are inspired by 'doing it yourself'. This theme is explored through exploration, play, songs and storytelling. Grown-ups are encouraged to take part at home by hiding a safe, toddler-appropriate 'doing it yourself' toy or object inside a recycled box for them to reveal and explore with their toddler. Storytime is all about joining in with the words, as Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear help Big Bear by doing odd jobs around the house. But will they get them all done? Viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring the 'doing it yourself' theme too. Plus, The Circle Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with stretching and the Goodbye song.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: In a game of hide-and-seek, Kiri pretends to be a flower.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Rebecca and Keith, Fine Forest’s best friends, have fallen out. Fred calls the Piggies for help. Fixing a friendship is harder than building!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Ted and his family head to the harbour and have fun trying to catch crabs. Will the crustacean critters be tempted by the bacon bait? Back home, Ted helps Dad clean Mum’s car, and then they make delicious spaghetti and meatballs for the whole family.

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Peggy is judging an art contest, but a storm puts it in jeopardy. Can Stan save the day? And who will win the competition?

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers arrive on the Magnetic Planet but can't play submarines - they just float in the air because they're not made of metal! They have to come up with creative ways to play the game.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: A snowstorm drives Ginger and the Pea-Rexes into a cave. Vegesaurs join them, which keeps spirits high.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Yellow is happy to bring his colour to Colourland. Learn about the colour yellow with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: It’s recycling day in the attic – and it's also Murphi’s hairdo day! The first idea is a hilarious hairdo pot, the Mini Monsters make a variety of cheese box octopuses, and the Magic Monster Mirror brings a call from Rebecca’s aunt. Finally, the Recycling Express arrives with some buttons that Murphi and Rebecca use to create a brilliant box robot.

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: An invisible troublemaker is causing mayhem in Peak City.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers learn why leaf piles are important for wildlife. They make their own, raking up the fallen leaves from the garden before getting creative! They make their leaf pile into some beautiful artwork, while at the same time creating a habitat for lots of local wildlife.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Jen is studying the poop of different dinosaurs on the island, so Andy heads out on an epic adventure to collect some samples. Along the way, he meets an Alamosaurus.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Introducing Squirrel Club today are Betty and Guinea Pig, jumping up and down, excited about what’s to come. Delivery Chipmunk delivers a massive parcel to Hennie, a Matryoshka Duggee appears, and there's an instalment of Agony and Eggstacy. Finally, Hatsu describes everything she likes - large, small, quiet, loud... Hatsu can see beauty in everything.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and the children weave trees from wool on paper plates, learn signs for wool, bags and lane, and sing and sign Baa Baa Black Sheep.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes must teach a lost baby Bokchoydactyl how to fly.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick, Remie and Alva are growing bean plants, but Norman's plant isn’t growing. Nick and the Popcasters suggest what Norman needs to do to get his beans back on the scene.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Koa’s nails are long and sharp, but he’s afraid to cut them. Vida knows just how to make it fun - nail polish!

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Big Lizard frustrates Dad by stealing a strange plant from the ship. A disaster is averted when Big Lizard persuades Dad that there's more to this plant than meets the eye - and nose...

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: At the bring-and-buy sale, Rafi insists on keeping her oldest toy, Tommy the T rex. But after a busy day, she realises he’s gone. Worried, she makes a wish to find him, and her wishing wand whisks her and Jake on a wild chase through the park. Finally, back at the bakery, they discover baby Oscar happily playing with Tommy - Amy bought it to cheer him up. Seeing Oscar’s joy, Rafi decides to let him keep Tommy.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran take the bus to visit the art gallery. JoJo wants to find paintings of pandas, so they join a tour with curator Marie and see lots of different type of art, and experience how abstract art makes them feel. JoJo can’t find any paintings of pandas but realises art isn't just for looking at – it's for making too! JoJo makes lots of panda art and creates her own gallery in Gran Gran's garden.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Bug's plant is looking droopy, but his button collecting seems to be the cause of the problem...

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Children's animation about Charlie's imaginative little sister Lola. Charlie and Lola's well-rehearsed circus act for Granny and Grandpa is put in jeopardy when poor Charlie breaks his arm playing football with Marv. Lola and Soren Lorensen try to nurse him back to health and cheer him up. But will Lola find anything for broken Charlie to do in the circus?

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: Little Nana and Lambkin play with the great big tub, until it rolls away with Little Nana inside. Hurry, Lambkin! Catch the great big tub!

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa have fun pretending to be different animals and making animal noises. At the Play Tree, they play with Purple Ducky and love making it squeak. When the squeak breaks, MeMo wants to find another toy to play with, but BaBa shows MeMo that they can still play with Purple Ducky. They take it to see the Yummies and their friends on the Lullaby Lake.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read stories. Igglepiggle discovers musical stepping stones. The Tombliboos hear Igglepiggle's stones, and then they hear Upsy Daisy singing. The Tombliboos go home and play music as well, very loudly! Makka Pakka must use his trumpet through Upsy Daisy's megaphone before the Tombliboos can hear him.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Adventure into the wild with Mr Motivator in this Bedtime Story.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Red and Blue compete to colour a castle and meet new arrival Purple. Discover what happens when you mix red and blue with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona really wants to learn how to jump like the experts.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Pando is teaching Bing and Sula how to do little kicks and big kicks with a ball in the garden. Sula does the biggest kick of them all, but Bing kicks the ball the wrong way. As he tries to kick it back to Pando it bounces off the shed, breaking Flop's window! They have to stand statue-still while Flop cleans up the glass.

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: Love Monster tries to share an old disco ball with his friends, but they all want to do different things with it.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Fred and Dana's door makes a squeaky sound, so they call the Piggy Builders to fix it. The Piggies decide to upgrade the entire door. They build the greatest door ever, but then forget how to open it.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: On a hot summer’s day, Ginger and the Peas try to find the perfect spot on the beach.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the body-drumming sensation, Watermelon! If she ever gets ripe and ready to perform.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Preston needs Mojo’s racer top speed to get his new plane off the ground. But when his flight goes wrong, Mojo and Bo have to take to the air in Mojo’s jet top to help him down!

programme.title: Chuggington
programme.desc: The trainees learn that with a little imagination any ordinary job can be extraordinary.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato and Broccoli go on a pirate adventure with Captain Pak Choi, but they don't realise she intends on plundering Evil Pea's freezer and stealing all her shiny things.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: 'Even when something breaks, you have to tell the truth so Flop knows what happened.' Bing is playing the talking lettuce game on Flop's phone when he drops the phone and accidentally breaks it. Too panicked to tell Flop what he has done, Bing puts the phone in the bin, but he's so upset that Flop knows something has happened.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Sula are building a stone tower in the Howly Woods when Sula finds an ammonite. Bing wants to find one too but is overwhelmed by the amount of stones, which makes it very difficult to find one. A frustrated Bing sits down, and Sula notices some ammonites in the rock behind him. Flop takes a picture of Bing and Sula with their ammonites.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After watching the birds fly above them, the Squirrels discover that birds can also slide, run and lay eggs. This encourages them to learn more about the natural environment, and they discover how to do this responsibly with Duggee’s five easy steps: watch carefully, stay at a distance, don’t interfere, be patient and alert, and stay quiet. The Squirrels embark on their own individual discoveries outside in rivers, the sea, mountains, the jungle and the desert. They learn how to spot an animal’s disguise, better known as its camouflage. They see how birds may try to impress one another, which is in stark contrast to how a horned lizard uses its body to warn other creatures off. A fascinating look at nature!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are hungry, but they’re not sure what to eat to fill their tummies, so they turn to Duggee for help. Fortunately, he has his cookbook The Clubhouse Kitchen: Tasty Bites for Hungry Squirrels, and together they pick out something they’d like. They decide the nut roast takes too long to make, and although cheetah toast is quicker, they don’t like getting raisins stuck in their teeth. Once they’ve picked a recipe, Duggee teaches them how to complete it: get the ingredients, prepare them and then put it together. After making some fun mess in the kitchen and a great cooking lesson, the Squirrels get to complete the last step together and eat what they made. Delicious!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: After a pod of pilot whales becomes stranded at the Academy beach, the Go Jetters, with help from new teacher Professor Wave, must work fast to return them to the ocean deeps. programme.desc: Ted and his family head to the harbour and have fun trying to catch crabs. Will the crustacean critters be tempted by the bacon bait? Back home, Ted helps Dad clean Mum’s car, and then they make delicious spaghetti and meatballs for the whole family.

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Peggy is judging an art contest, but a storm puts it in jeopardy. Can Stan save the day? And who will win the competition?

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers arrive on the Magnetic Planet but can't play submarines - they just float in the air because they're not made of metal! They have to come up with creative ways to play the game.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: A snowstorm drives Ginger and the Pea-Rexes into a cave. Vegesaurs join them, which keeps spirits high.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Yellow is happy to bring his colour to Colourland. Learn about the colour yellow with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: It’s recycling day in the attic – and it's also Murphi’s hairdo day! The first idea is a hilarious hairdo pot, the Mini Monsters make a variety of cheese box octopuses, and the Magic Monster Mirror brings a call from Rebecca’s aunt. Finally, the Recycling Express arrives with some buttons that Murphi and Rebecca use to create a brilliant box robot.

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: An invisible troublemaker is causing mayhem in Peak City.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers learn why leaf piles are important for wildlife. They make their own, raking up the fallen leaves from the garden before getting creative! They make their leaf pile into some beautiful artwork, while at the same time creating a habitat for lots of local wildlife.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Jen is studying the poop of different dinosaurs on the island, so Andy heads out on an epic adventure to collect some samples. Along the way, he meets an Alamosaurus.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Introducing Squirrel Club today are Betty and Guinea Pig, jumping up and down, excited about what’s to come. Delivery Chipmunk delivers a massive parcel to Hennie, a Matryoshka Duggee appears, and there's an instalment of Agony and Eggstacy. Finally, Hatsu describes everything she likes - large, small, quiet, loud... Hatsu can see beauty in everything.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and the children weave trees from wool on paper plates, learn signs for wool, bags and lane, and sing and sign Baa Baa Black Sheep.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes must teach a lost baby Bokchoydactyl how to fly.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick, Remie and Alva are growing bean plants, but Norman's plant isn’t growing. Nick and the Popcasters suggest what Norman needs to do to get his beans back on the scene.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Koa’s nails are long and sharp, but he’s afraid to cut them. Vida knows just how to make it fun - nail polish!

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Big Lizard frustrates Dad by stealing a strange plant from the ship. A disaster is averted when Big Lizard persuades Dad that there's more to this plant than meets the eye - and nose...

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: At the bring-and-buy sale, Rafi insists on keeping her oldest toy, Tommy the T rex. But after a busy day, she realises he’s gone. Worried, she makes a wish to find him, and her wishing wand whisks her and Jake on a wild chase through the park. Finally, back at the bakery, they discover baby Oscar happily playing with Tommy - Amy bought it to cheer him up. Seeing Oscar’s joy, Rafi decides to let him keep Tommy.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran take the bus to visit the art gallery. JoJo wants to find paintings of pandas, so they join a tour with curator Marie and see lots of different type of art, and experience how abstract art makes them feel. JoJo can’t find any paintings of pandas but realises art isn't just for looking at – it's for making too! JoJo makes lots of panda art and creates her own gallery in Gran Gran's garden.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Bug's plant is looking droopy, but his button collecting seems to be the cause of the problem...

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Children's animation about Charlie's imaginative little sister Lola. Charlie and Lola's well-rehearsed circus act for Granny and Grandpa is put in jeopardy when poor Charlie breaks his arm playing football with Marv. Lola and Soren Lorensen try to nurse him back to health and cheer him up. But will Lola find anything for broken Charlie to do in the circus?

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: Little Nana and Lambkin play with the great big tub, until it rolls away with Little Nana inside. Hurry, Lambkin! Catch the great big tub!

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa have fun pretending to be different animals and making animal noises. At the Play Tree, they play with Purple Ducky and love making it squeak. When the squeak breaks, MeMo wants to find another toy to play with, but BaBa shows MeMo that they can still play with Purple Ducky. They take it to see the Yummies and their friends on the Lullaby Lake.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read stories. Igglepiggle discovers musical stepping stones. The Tombliboos hear Igglepiggle's stones, and then they hear Upsy Daisy singing. The Tombliboos go home and play music as well, very loudly! Makka Pakka must use his trumpet through Upsy Daisy's megaphone before the Tombliboos can hear him.

programme.title: Mamma Mia!
programme.desc: Romantic musical comedy. An independent single mother who owns a small hotel on the idyllic Greek isle of Kalokairi, Donna is about to let go of Sophie, the spirited daughter she's raised alone. Donna has invited her two life-long best girlfriends - practical, no-nonsense Rosie and wealthy multi-divorcee Tanya - from her one-time backing band Donna and the Dynamos for Sophie's wedding... and Sophie has secretly invited three guests of her own in a quest to find the identity of her father. To walk her down the aisle, Sophie brings back three men from Donna's past to the Mediterranean paradise that they visited 20 years earlier - new love will bloom and old romances will rekindle over 24 hours on a lush island full of possibilities... and the whole story is told through the music of ABBA.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot O'Leary's culinary adventure takes him west to Ballycastle, a former Viking settlement and a jewel of the Causeway Coastal Route. With Rathlin Island on the horizon, Dermot heads out on a wildlife-watching trip, spotting seabirds and seals while uncovering the area's rich history. Back on shore and hungry from the sea air, he joins bakers Ciara and Dara at Ursa Minor, where they bake a blueberry pie using local fruit and a clever twist - infusing pastry with vanilla-tasting fig leaves, as the real thing won't grow on the island. Dessert comes first before Dermot heads inland to Broughgammon Farm. Here, husband-and-wife team Charlie and Becky are reshaping local food culture, championing goat meat and rose veal while giving value to male animals from the dairy industry. Dermot meets the animals and learns to cook the couple's favourite dish: schnitzel.
